segments.text: Hello and welcome to Editors Unplugged.
Madhav Das, Gopalakrishnan, Siddharth, Talia, Pragya, Kaushika are now joining us today.
Let's start with a couple of things that a lot of people are talking about on social media and otherwise.
One is the CJP protests, the chatter around it.
The vote-chori march led by Rahul Gandhi, supported by some opposition parties or most opposition parties.
And the other is about the Javer airport, the Noida airport being renamed.
So, you know, let's start with the CJP and then we'll come to the airport bit.
Madhav, the unprecedented security measures, curbs put in place by the Delhi police.
is grabbing a lot of attention, eyeballs.
What do you make of it?

Because the last time when the protests happened, when there was all this violence outside of parliament, in fact, tear gas being fired in so many places, whether it's Rafi Mark, whether it's, you know, Ashok Road, that entire area of central Delhi where we saw the kind of protests take place.
The big question that people were asking is what was the intelligence doing?
What was the police doing?
Why couldn't they have sort of nipped it in the bud rather than let
say 10-15,000 or however many protesters came in over there.
So this time they have decided to obviously take that advice rather seriously.
And they've had several days of preparation.
CJP has not kept its plan secret exactly.
We are seeing CJP leaders come out to say that thousands of people have been arrested around the country, whether that's an exaggeration or not.
It is a fact that trains have been stopped.
Several trains at that.
Is that arrest?
Preventive detention?
What is it?
Well, they claim that they've been detained.
Detention, yeah, it's detention.
Obviously, legally speaking, you're right, it's detention, not arrest as such.
But the point is that the crackdown is a problem.
The crackdown will become, now we don't know which is going to be worse, because if those protesters do actually read Jantar Mantar and they do come, what will happen in a situation like that?
We've already seen what the opposition parties, the India Bloc and Congress has already been saying that they were not allowed to go to Jantar Mantar.
Hence, we saw that jostling, the push and pulling that took place.
Are we looking at a similar kind of situation in the National Capital next few days?
And this time around, the permissions have been explicitly denied on the part of the Delhi Police.
Yeah, the police said that it was at a very short notice.
It was at a very short notice.

They've also cited precedent over the fact that the CJP defied instructions that they had been given the previous time round and going by their track record, they're not in a position to trust the CJP to carry out a peaceful protest.
That's pretty much what the police has said in a nutshell.

The question, of course, arises as to whether or not they've actually gone into an overdrive and they've gone a bit overboard when it comes to the preparations, but they can always justify it by saying that you never know what's going to happen.
So we have to take all the preparatory steps.
Prajya, how is the government looking at this?

First, Rahul Gandhi, you know, hitting the streets, you know, almost now on a daily basis, over the last 3-4 days, first they go out for lunch, then there is brainstorming there, then they go on the road, they wanted to meet the CEC, that also didn't happen.
They are saying that Narendra Modi must resign.
Well, you know, government is obviously not happy with all of this, but they cannot stop opposition from protesting.
You know, if they do that, then everyone will say that this is an autocratic government, which is the opposition is saying and you will prove that point.
So they do not want to stop opposition members.
But they're saying one thing.
If you do not have trust in Supreme Court, then who do you trust?
They also need this reply from leader of opposition.
He's not just Rahul Gandhi and MP.
He's also leader of opposition.
So if the battle is already in Supreme Court and Supreme Court is already hearing it, please have some patience, wait.
You know, the better, you know, advice someone could have given Rahul Gandhi is to fight this battle inside the court.
You know, every time they take a matter like EVMs to court, they fail miserably.
This time, many of them... Every time that happens and you know, the narrative of the
The opposition's narrative fizzles, so to say, for lack of a better word.
They get called out.
In this case, the Congress party is wanting to make the Chief Election Commissioner.
Is that a big ask?
It is a very big ask, but having said that, Election Commissioner is not responsible to Leader of Opposition.
He's responsible to President of India.
And he is supposed to be very neutral in conducting free and fair elections.
He cannot come under undue pressure from anyone, be it government or be it from opposition.
But I'm just making a point, you know, if you have solid evidence, you have 6.8 BLAs all over the country.
What were they doing?
Not even a single objection.
You do not file complaint, you do not file appeal.
I spoke to one of the leaders, Pranav Jha, who was fielded for Rajya Sabha candidate.
He said, you know, it is like, I said, why did your BLAs not object?
So his explanation was that, you know, if there is a loot in our house or a theft in our house, should the government be not made or police not be made responsible?
Should they tell us that we need to lock our house?
Obviously, you need to lock your houses.
You know, this is no explanation.
Yeah.
BJP has BLAs.
They are making it a point in Uttar Pradesh to ensure that their voters are included in the electoral roll.
There is a bit of a chicken and egg problem.
I'll just explain this.

So what happens is there is an inbuilt mechanism in the SIR which is that all the parties have their boot level agents who are supposed to monitor those lists and if there are discrepancies point them out and access the system.
What is happening now in the case of Bengal and Bihar

yes there are huge violations of procedure that have been documented and in fact the express report and what has come for supreme court also no problems with the website with the form six modalities etc etc but what is also true is that opposition political parties are not robustly complaining and
sort of exercising the powers that they already have because their argument is that we don't have faith in the election commission, we don't have faith in the system, the system is rigged, etc.
But there is a little bit of responsibility, as Pragya says, on opposition parties also to ensure that that system works.
Has the SIR process been hurried?
Perhaps it has.
Have there been a lot of arbitrary steps that have been taken and does the website not function properly?
Going by what, you know, the Kolkata judicial officers as well as the Goa bench of the Bombay High Court has said, I think that seems to be quite apparent now and there definitely need to be changes.
But does that mean that opposition political parties boycott that process completely and is that justified?
That becomes a very big question.
And I'm sure this will come out before Supreme Court.
Use that to demand the resignation of the Prime Minister, Siddharth.
Is that a bit of a stretch or, you know, it is normal political posturing?
This is normal political posturing and let's also not forget there's a huge amount of selectivity involved when it comes to the opposition because the SIR was conducted in multiple states.
The Congress did end up winning the state of Kerala for example.
In Tamil Nadu where there was also an SIR exercise that was conducted, the TVK of course came to power but the Congress is very much now part
of the ruling dispensation there as an alliance partner.
So they've of course gone hammer and tongs as and when they found an opportunity to corner the BJP.
However, as and when it suited them, they've been conspicuously silent.
There's another aspect to all of this in terms of the kind of protest that we witnessed.
Obviously, Rahul Gandhi is also trying to steal the CJP's thunder in the buildup to
of what was being planned on the 10th of October, the kind of street level politics that we've seen in this latest instance, nor that he's not done it before.
He wanted to essentially preempt any possible impact that he saw the CJP having.
But I think his anger is not against Gyanesh Kumar so much but it is against Narendra Modi and also Amit Shah.
I think the ultimate objective is that and in fact they are using ECI to attack Prime Minister.
But what are you hearing from, you know, people in power about Gyanesh Kumar?
They have increased security, that's okay, nobody is, you know, grudging him that.
But people are asking questions, this is a press conference, answer them.
This is not just about Rahul Gandhi, it's about, you know, ensuring trust in the general public.
But then, Pranesh, there is also another factor.
Remember when there were allegations of the same SIR electoral rolls previously on Mr. Gyanesh Kumar?
Gyanesh Kumar did call up opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi.
And they chose not to go.
And they sent you on two occasions.
Last year and this year, there were two occasions.
And in fact, he said that you sit with me across the table.
No, I agree.
We had also told stories that this is not responsible behavior on part of the opposition.
But is that being used as a, you know, justification now?
There is one problem in that.
And you see, I completely agree with the fact that all our Constitutional Court, Supreme Court, High Court, and that comes up in our debates, they've cleared the EVM so many times.
And that's why the VVPAT was brought in.
In fact, when LK Advani complained, what is the logical result of all of that?
Judicially speaking, then you brought in a machine called the VVPAT where there's a print
Extra layer of check.
It's an extra layer of check and then the counting of VVPATs becomes an issue.
Even that went to the courts.
So all that back and forth is fine for any democracy.
Obviously people aren't going to sit silent.
There needs to be debate.
There needs to be discussion and that's how we improve our system.
To that extent what the opposition doing is perfectly fine.
This time around though there have been a series of violations and the manner in which election commission functions has come under a question.
For instance, the very fact that two ECs had to write to the cabinet secretary.
That's not a
routine of development, number one.
Number two, they're saying that we're not holding meetings regularly.
So that is also something that Mr. Gyanesh Kumar has to account for.
Does this mean that necessarily all the exercises and everything that is happening is malified?
Perhaps not.
But there definitely needs to be accountability fixed within the system.
How the courts are going to do that needs to be seen.
But the level of violations this time around that are being reported certainly calls for, you know, some amount of introspection on part of election.
Whether or not Gyanesh Kumar owes an audience to the opposition parties that are protesting is one debate.

But the very fact that some inane press releases have been issued following, of course, the publication of the report on the part of EC sources and even formal press releases, they've not answered all the questions that have been raised.
So he definitely owes a lot of responses over the questions that have been asked of him.
He should hold a press conference, which he hasn't.
I'll just add one last point is that the very fact that the EC press release of 26 September
It changes the position of EC on many things.
At least on seven or eight points they've clarified in that particular press release.
Since then they've announced special drives, voter inclusion drives.
What does all this mean?
It is also an admission of many things.
Another layer of confusion that they've added in that September 26 press release when they said that the Form 6 had been upheld on the part of the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court in that judgment of May 2026 had also added a caveat, etc.
I was speaking to Harish on this, I was speaking to our legal editor Harish on this.
So Harish's point of view is that both Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commission are right and the Supreme Court is right.
So I said why is that?
He says because both are talking about two different things.
Yeah, absolutely.
The Supreme Court is talking about the form not being modified and they are talking about an addition in the form of... But beyond the technicalities, you know, perception is everything in politics.
You're right Puneesh, perception is everything.
But you know Ganesh Kumar did agree to meet them even when they went to Akashwani Bhavan.
But they said that the request came only at 4 o'clock and there was a caveat to that.
That you have to meet all 240 of us in Parliament and XE.
That would also create this mistrust.
That you can't ask President Murmu to step out of Rashtrapati Bhavan and hold it.
opposition functionaries have a place.

The election commission's job is to ensure that there are free and fair elections in this country and they are the ones who ensure that the people who sit in the legislature get there in a particular way.
Now to expect the CEC to come to parliament is quite probable.
But the opposition was being charitable.
They said that parliament should come to NHC or else they would say that the decision should be made on Janatar Mantar.
Here, Dipke and the others will preside.
First of all, 240 is questionable, whosoever was there.
Last time, Nadda ji was seen hobnobbing with Dipke and others.
Nadda ji, will you go to receive them?
Or what will be their role this time?
I think they'll stay clear of Dipke this time.
And in fact, for that matter, Jiten Singh also.
They have been very amicable faces of the government.
You know, acceptability on all sides.
The government tried in good faith, but yeah.
But there's a lot of trust deficit and not just trust deficit.
I think the government also has some sort of intel on these people.
And in fact, what many in the power corridors are saying that because Aam Aadmi Party has lost credibility, they need something, some
other wing.
So CJP is the B team of the Aam Aadmi party.
But that we also saw on you know social media as well.
There's a spat between Congress leaders and you know Saurav Das as well where Congress leaders said that you are part of Aam Aadmi party.
We also know that you came.
The very fact that we are missing the most important part while we are talking about vote chori.
The Supreme Court has ordered fresh polls in 50 municipal votes in Punjab.
And all these safe democracy saviours, Deepki and others, and even the foreign YouTubers are not saying one thing.
This is worse than stealing votes.
Exactly.
So that is of course definitely an important thing, but what is I think highlighted in this entire point that both of you were just making is the friction between AAP and Congress.
Because it's quite evident, AAP has not attended the India Block protest through the week.
They said that we'll protest together at the CEO's office and that also collapsed.
And now you have Kejriwal and others who are asking people to go and join the 10th October protest.
Well, they have not been part of this protest.
So that friction is there.
They're going to fight it out again in Punjab.
So I think all of that is also... Let's see how that plays out.
The other thing that, you know, we should be discussing is the renaming of the or rather the naming of the...
Noida Airport, because it was not even named till now.
The name of it was Narendra Modi Airport.
Yogi Adityanath, the Chief Minister made the announcement.
Was it going to happen?
Was it in the works, Pragya?
Or this came as a surprise to you too?
Now, this was a sentiment in UP government that this airport came into existence because of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's effort, because there was a lot of traffic on Delhi airport.
You needed one in NCR.
So, Jaipur was the place that has been decided.
But now cabinet has officially approved the name of this particular airport and they believe that
It is a befitting tribute to Prime Minister's 25 years of, you know, continuous public service.
He has given a lot to country, lot of development, you know, taken out 25 crore people out of poverty, so much of financial independence to Lakhpati Didis.

So all of that, so I think probably the reason why they decided, this is also a, you know, Seva Sankalp Deva Sabhiyan that BJP is running, you know, in wake of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's birthday and October 7th was when... Predictably, you know, the opposition is saying what it is.
Mahatma Sir, is that a problem?
Well, we saw the politics around Narendra Modi stadium.
So why do you expect that there won't be politics around Narendra Modi airport?
I think that is obviously part of the game.
It's inevitable.
And obviously, they will have problems with the fact that it's a serving PM, etc., who will be named.
All those problems will be there.
But again, the counter will come that what about Indira Gandhi International Airport, which is the main airport of New Delhi.
That's named after a prime minister from the Congress party.
that political back and forth is of course going to play out as far as the name change politics is concerned.
But the way I look at it is another interesting aspect that ahead of UP elections, remember the prime minister is the biggest brand name, the biggest vote puller as far as the BJP is concerned.
So paying tribute to him is in some sense securing that and ensuring that the state government, the central government are all aligned as far as the UP elections are concerned.
It also has impacts on within the BJP and its own politics because here's
Yogi coming out to very strongly back the Prime Minister.
You know, that is also sending out a signal to everybody else as far as... Everyone's on the same page.
Exactly, that they're on the same page, that they're together.
And of course the dynamics, within every party there are dynamics that play out internally.
I think this is going to have a huge amount of internal... You remember the commentary around, you know, the naming of that stadium in Gujarat.
Correct.
Yeah, so we know the controversy that took place then but there's a slight distinction, Madhav.

The thing is the Congress will... will counter the BJP by saying that as far as the Indira Gandhi International Airport is concerned or the naming of Indira point which is the southernmost point in India in the Andamans or for that matter the naming of Jawaharlal Nehru University.
All these took place after the respective leaders had died.
But that can't be... Yeah, that can't be a justification.
You can't wait for someone, can you?
Let's also not forget that there are thousands of institutions, other places, locations that have been named.
So when it comes to the UPA and the Congress, absolutely, 100%, I totally agree with you.
When it comes to Congress, it's psychofancy on steroids.
There's absolutely no two ways about it.
But that's how they'll counter that while a prime minister is still serving,
Is it really appropriate to have an institution like this or a piece of infrastructure to be named after him while he is still serving as PM?
The Congress will claim that we did a lot of this in terms of naming certain locations etc.
while a lot of these leaders had moved on.
However, the counter to that also is the Congress was quite brazen.
Let's also not forget that when it came to the Bharat Ratna, both Jawaharlal Nehru and Indira Gandhi got it while they were still in service.
Is there sentiment in this party?
Party is happy.
Party stands behind Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Prime Minister Narendra Modi is also an MP from Uttar Pradesh.
So I think this has every imprint of UP polls as Madhav was saying that Prime Minister is the only vote puller in the party.
He can swing both at the end of the moment when there are, you know, there have been instances we had seen in the past where party has requested him.
And in fact, he has requested party, please use me wherever you want to use me.
Give me five rallies a day.
I'll do it.
I don't mind.
So he's the one leading from the front.
And Uttar Pradesh is a electorally very significant state.
You know, if you want to come to power in Central, it's a prestige battle and they can't lose it.

and they're waiting for you know also congress to lose Uttar Pradesh because they believe the what party is believing is that this whole protest of Rahul Gandhi is going to continue not just till winter session it is going to continue till Uttar Pradesh elections.

The renaming?

In parliament as well, he does that.

in the day that you know samajwadi party is the main opposition looks like a main opposition party right now when it comes to the issues against government but very interestingly what many of the congress leaders are also believing is that the difference and you know the sort of

Rahul Gandhi's respond.

BJP people.
